pharm: Topical anti-proliferative agent for chronic plaque psoriasis
quick: Apply thin layer to plaques once daily; short-contact (10-30 min then wash off), concentration escalated as tolerated
Limited data; minimal systemic absorption - use only if clearly needed, avoid extensive use
Minimal systemic absorption; avoid application to breast and prevent infant contact with treated skin
Local irritation/burning, skin staining, treatment response
summary: Liposomal dithranol (anthralin) is a topical anti-psoriatic hydroxyanthrone in which the active is encapsulated in liposomes to improve cutaneous delivery and reduce the characteristic skin staining and irritation seen with conventional dithranol. It is used for chronic plaque psoriasis, applied to plaques - frequently as short-contact therapy (e.g., 10-30 minutes then washed off) with stepwise concentration escalation. It is anti-proliferative, normalizing keratinocyte hyperproliferation and differentiation with anti-inflammatory effects. Brown-purple staining of skin, clothing and bathtub, and perilesional burning/irritation are the principal limitations; the face, flexures, genitals and eyes must be avoided. It is not suitable for acute, pustular or inflamed psoriasis. The liposomal form is investigational/non-US and is NOT FDA-approved.
indications: Topical treatment of chronic stable plaque psoriasis
Localized plaque psoriasis where short-contact dithranol therapy is appropriate

dosage.d: Apply to plaques starting at a low concentration, leave 10-30 minutes, then wash off; increase contact time/concentration stepwise as tolerated
dosage.n: Begin low and titrate up; stop escalation if irritation occurs

dosage.d: Apply thin film to plaques and leave in place (e.g., overnight) per protocol
dosage.n: Higher staining/irritation risk than short-contact; reserve for resistant plaques

dosage.c: Acute, pustular, erythrodermic or inflamed psoriasis
dosage.n: Risk of severe irritation and flare

admin: Apply only to well-defined plaques; protect surrounding normal skin (e.g., with a bland barrier such as petrolatum)
Wear gloves or use an applicator; wash hands thoroughly after application to avoid staining
For short-contact therapy, leave on for the prescribed time (commonly 10-30 minutes) then wash off thoroughly
Avoid the face, eyes, flexures, skin folds, genitals and mucous membranes
Expect transient brown-purple staining of skin, clothing, towels and bath surfaces; use old linens
moa: Dithranol (anthralin) is a hydroxyanthrone that exerts an anti-proliferative effect on the epidermis, reducing keratinocyte hyperproliferation and normalizing abnormal keratinocyte differentiation, together with anti-inflammatory activity. Its action is thought to involve mitochondrial dysfunction and generation of reactive oxygen species in keratinocytes, impairing cellular energy metabolism and DNA synthesis. Liposomal encapsulation modifies cutaneous delivery, aiming to enhance penetration into plaques while limiting the oxidative staining and irritation associated with free dithranol.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to dithranol/anthralin or formulation components
Application to inflamed or eroded skin
relative: Application near the face, flexures, genitals or eyes

preg: Human pregnancy data are limited. Systemic absorption after topical use is minimal, so systemic fetal exposure is expected to be low; nevertheless avoid extensive or prolonged use and use only if clearly needed. Avoid application to large body-surface areas during pregnancy.
lact: Systemic absorption is minimal and significant excretion into breast milk is not expected. Avoid applying to the breast/chest and prevent the infant from contacting treated skin to avoid staining and irritation.
renal: Systemic absorption is negligible; no renal dose adjustment is required.
hepatic: Systemic absorption is negligible; no hepatic dose adjustment is required.

moderate: Concurrent topical irritants or keratolytics (e.g., salicylic acid, tar, topical retinoids) - additive skin irritation
Phototherapy (UVB/PUVA) - may be combined under supervision but increases irritation/erythema risk
minor: Other topical products on the same area may alter penetration or staining
interactions.diagnostics: None significant; staining can transiently discolor treated skin and may be mistaken for pigmentation changes.

common: Skin irritation/burning at and around application site
Brown-purple staining of treated and perilesional skin
Staining of clothing, towels and bath surfaces
rare: Conjunctival irritation/staining if eye contact occurs
emergency: Severe allergic reaction (swelling, hives, difficulty breathing)

monitoring: Local tolerance - reduce concentration or contact time if burning/irritation is excessive
Degree of staining of treated and surrounding skin
Plaque response (scaling, thickness, erythema) over weeks
Spread of irritation beyond the plaque margin
counsel: Apply only to the thick plaques, not normal skin; protecting surrounding skin with petrolatum helps prevent irritation and staining
For short-contact use, wash off thoroughly after the prescribed time (often 10-30 minutes)
Expect brown-purple staining of skin (fades over days-weeks), clothing and bath - use old clothes and rinse the bath/shower promptly
Avoid the face, skin folds, genitals and eyes; wash hands well after applying
Report worsening burning or spreading redness; this signals over-strong treatment
pk: Plaque improvement over days to a few weeks of regular use
Maximal benefit typically over several weeks
Minimal systemic exposure; not clinically relevant (acts locally, rapidly oxidized in skin)
Sustained with continued application; staining resolves over days to weeks after stopping
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from light; keep liposomal preparation per product instructions and avoid freezing
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; dithranol/anthralin products are used in Europe/UK and the liposomal formulation is investigational/non-US
Liposomal encapsulation is intended to reduce the staining and irritation that limit conventional dithranol
Short-contact therapy (apply, wait 10-30 min, wash off) reduces staining and irritation while retaining efficacy
Always start at a low concentration and escalate slowly; protect perilesional skin with petrolatum
Not for acute, pustular or inflamed psoriasis, and never for the face, flexures, genitals or eyes
missed: If a once-daily application is missed, apply it when remembered the same day, or simply resume the next scheduled application; do not apply extra or use a higher concentration to compensate.
overdose: Excessive concentration, contact time or area causes intensified local irritation, burning and staining rather than systemic toxicity. Wash the area thoroughly, discontinue or step down to a lower concentration/shorter contact time, and soothe with bland emollients. Accidental ingestion is managed with standard supportive care.
